citation: Lesaux, N. K., Kieffer, M. J., Kelley, J. G., & Harris, J. R. (2014). Effects of academic vocabulary instruction for linguistically diverse adolescents: Evidence from a randomized field trial. American Educational Research Journal, 51(6), 1159-1194. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831214532165
report_number: American Educational Research Journal, 51(6), 1159-1194; DOI 10.3102/0002831214532165; IES Grant R305A080631; ERIC Grantee Submission ED630431
design: Cluster-randomized field trial (RCT); assignment at the TEACHER/CLASSROOM level within school blocks. 14 urban middle schools (large CA district); 50 teachers randomized (25 treatment / 25 control), 37 treatment sections / 39 control sections; 2,082 grade-6 students (971 treatment / 1,111 control; 71% language-minority). 20-week ALIAS academic-vocabulary curriculum delivered by teachers who were trained/supported to implement it (TPD for curricula); control = business-as-usual core ELA instruction. Subject = vocabulary/literacy (reading, morphology/language, writing). Grade 6 (registry grade band 3-6). Impact estimated with two-level HLM (students nested within teachers), pretest-adjusted.
problems: LEGAL OA SOURCE: Published article (SAGE/AERJ) is closed access per OpenAlex and Unpaywall (oa_status=closed, no oa_locations). Full text obtained from the legal IES/funder green-OA copy: ERIC Grantee Submission ED630431 (files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED630431.pdf), the author's accepted manuscript deposited under the IES public-access policy (Grant R305A080631), reproduced with publisher permission ('Copyright 2014 by AERA; reproduced with permission'). This is the SAME study (identical title, authors, abstract, Tables 1-3); 54-page manuscript. No piracy site used. NOTE: the Read-tool PDF renderer only rendered 8 of 54 pages; full text was extracted via pdftotext (pdfinfo confirms 54 pages, 633KB). | VARIANCE/SE NOT REPORTED: The paper reports treatment effects only as Cohen's d (Table 3) and unstandardized HLM coefficients (Table 2); it does NOT report standard errors, confidence intervals, or the standardizing SD for the d values, and gives no explicit effect-size formula. I verified that reported d = (HLM treatment coefficient gamma1 from Table 2) / (pooled posttest SD from Table 1) across all 8 outcomes (implied SD = b/d matches the pooled posttest SD to within ~2% for every outcome), so g_method below reflects the authors' own posttest-SD standardization of the pretest-adjusted two-level HLM impact coefficient. Because no SE is reported, g_var/g_se are APPROXIMATIONS: Var(d) = (nt+nc)/(nt*nc) + d^2/(2(nt+nc)) inflated by a design effect DEFF = 1 + (m-1)*ICC, using avg cluster size m = N/50 and the authors' AVERAGE teacher-level ICC = 0.17 (the paper reports teacher-level ICCs ranging .12-.21 across the 8 outcomes; exact per-outcome ICCs are not tabulated, so .17 is recorded as the design-effect ICC for all rows and the range is noted). The impact estimate itself is from the cluster-accounting two-level HLM, so cluster_adjusted=true; n_clusters=50 and icc are recorded so the variance can be re-derived centrally (Hedges 2007) if the design-effect approximation is unsatisfactory. | TIMEPOINT: single post-intervention wave (May 2009, end of 20-week treatment); no later follow-up. | SUBJECT MAPPING: vocabulary and reading-comprehension measures -> Reading; morphological-awareness (language/word-learning) and writing measures -> Other (per spec writing/language/other -> Other). | INDEPENDENT vs RESEARCHER-MADE: only Gates-MacGinitie Reading Comprehension and OWLS Written Expression are standardized/independent (the measures the meta-analysis would retain); the other six are researcher-developed and curriculum-aligned (extracted and labeled per spec; filter centrally). | All 8 effect sizes are full-sample 'Overall' treatment effects (Table 3). The paper also reports LM/EO and pretest-vocabulary-quartile subgroup effects (Table 3) and student-by-treatment interactions; those subgroups are NOT extracted (is_full_sample would be false). | Pretest descriptive stats (Table 1) are reported only for Academic Word Mastery, Morphological Derivation, and Gates-MacGinitie; posttest means/SDs are reported for all outcomes. mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c below are the posttest OS (overall-sample) values from Table 1.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ALIAS academic-vocabulary curriculum (teachers trained to implement) vs business-as-usual core ELA
effect_sizes.test_name: Gates-MacGinitie Reading Test, 4th Ed.: Reading Comprehension (Form T, equated extended scaled scores)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d; d = 0.04 = authors' Cohen's d (Table 3, p.50/Table3), = HLM treatment coefficient gamma1 = 1.43 (Table 2) divided by pooled posttest SD (~33.1, from Table 1 posttest OS SDs 33.96/32.38). Two-level HLM (students within teachers), pretest-adjusted (Gates pretest covariate). J = 1-3/(4*df-1) with df = nt+nc-2 = 2080, J~0.99964. g_var approximated = [ (nt+nc)/(nt*nc) + d^2/(2(nt+nc)) ] * DEFF, DEFF = 1+(m-1)*ICC, m=2082/50=41.6, ICC=0.17 (avg teacher-level ICC) -> DEFF=7.91; no SE reported by authors.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3 'Overall' row (Gates MacGinitie Reading Comprehension), p. ~50 of MS / AERJ pp.1159-1194; Table 2 coefficient 1.43; Table 1 posttest OS means/SDs; results text p.31-32 of MS (d=0.04, p=.4256)
effect_sizes.notes: The ONLY standardized/independent reading-comprehension achievement measure and the closest 'far-transfer' outcome. Not statistically significant (d=0.04, p=.4256). This is the outcome most aligned with the meta-analysis's independent-measure inclusion criterion. Pretest covariate = Gates pretest (student- and teacher-mean centered).

effect_sizes.arm_label: ALIAS academic-vocabulary curriculum (teachers trained to implement) vs business-as-usual core ELA
effect_sizes.test_name: Oral and Written Language Scales (OWLS): Written Expression (Carrow-Woolfolk 1996)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d; d = 0.19 = authors' Cohen's d (Table 3) = HLM coefficient 2.15 (Table 2) / pooled posttest SD (~11.06, Table 1 SDs 10.51/11.54). Pretest-adjusted two-level HLM (Gates pretest covariate; OWLS had no pretest). df = nt+nc-2 = 744, J~0.99899. g_var approx = simple-Var(d)*DEFF; writing was a random within-class subsample so m=746/50=14.9, DEFF=1+(14.9-1)*0.17=3.37; no SE reported.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3 'Overall' (Written Expression), n=746; Table 2 coefficient 2.15 (n=746); Table 1 posttest OS means/SDs; results text p.31-32 of MS (d=0.19, p=.0388)
effect_sizes.notes: Standardized/independent WRITING measure (subject -> Other per spec). Significant overall (d=0.19, p=.0388) but NOT significant in the complete-case (non-imputed) reduced sample (authors note this, attributed to lower power). Administered to a random within-classroom subsample only (n=746; 357 T / 389 C). No writing pretest; HLM controlled for Gates pretest comprehension.
